Continuity · Collected edition

Continuity: The Complete Trilogy

The world didn't end. It froze.

When a stellar black hole passes through the Solar System, Earth is torn from its orbit. The oceans turn to ice, whole nations vanish beneath it, and what remains of humanity retreats into the United Nations Continuity Programme: a network of underground refuges built to carry civilisation through the dark.

But refuges fail, and the cold is here to stay.

For Commander Robert Dixon and his family, safety lies a continent away, beyond a frozen wasteland where every mile has a price. Their destination is the Rift Valley, humanity's greatest stronghold. The road that takes them there will shape the future of the human race.

An epic of survival, sacrifice and hope.

The Last Orbits of Man · Book One

The Last Orbits of Man: Descent

Out 15 December 2026 · Kindle & paperback

Earth has been silent for twenty-four years. Now someone is calling for help.

Read the full blurb

Earth has been silent for twenty-four years. Now someone is calling for help.

When the Bakali invaded, humanity lost its fleets, its cities and its home. Then the aliens released a pathogen that transformed billions of people into creatures still roaming the ruins.

The survivors fled to four distant space stations. Hidden across the solar system, they live aboard ageing machinery, protected by the few warships that escaped the invasion. Every patrol risks discovery. Every year, the Bakali return.

A transmission from beneath the Swiss Alps reveals that a group of scientists and marines has survived inside the Lazarus Facility. Their power is failing, their supplies are dwindling, and they cannot reach the surface alone. But they possess something that could give humanity a way to fight back.

For the crew of UES Prometheus, the last surviving Titan-class command carrier, the message means preparing for a mission few expected to make: a return to Earth.

Reaching the facility will mean crossing enemy-controlled space and sending troops into a world abandoned to the transformed. Committing ships to the rescue will leave the stations vulnerable—and the Bakali must never learn where humanity has been hiding.

The people inside Lazarus have waited twenty-four years for an answer. Humanity’s remaining fleet may have only one chance to reach them.

Meet the author

Joseph R
Holdsworth.

Big ideas. Human stories.

I’m an independent author from Wales, also known as J.R.H. I write about humanity’s survival, strange discoveries and the worlds we might one day find ourselves in.

My inspirations include A.G. Riddle, Isaac Asimov and Stephen Baxter. Away from writing, I’m an enthusiastic Pokémon card collector.

Why I write ↓

In my own words

Why am I
an author?

A love of stories.
An overactive imagination.
A reason to keep writing.

Well, it’s simple: I love stories, and I love all things creative.

Growing up, I always had an overactive imagination. I was born with dyslexia, dyscalculia, and dyspraxia, and later in life was diagnosed as a high-functioning autistic male.

I think when someone is neurodivergent, one of our greatest strengths is creativity. That’s not to say neurotypical people aren’t creative, but I do believe those of us who are neurodivergent focus deeply on the fine details, how things work, and making sure everything fits together just right. When I write my novels, it’s not just about getting a good concept onto the page—it’s about exploring why things are the way they are, from anomalies and survival rationing to the intricate inner workings of the world itself.

Since I started bringing my novels to the world, it has been an incredible experience. I genuinely believe being an independent author is the best way to do it. You get the raw, unfiltered imagination of the author's mind, rather than something filtered through professional ghostwriters or rewritten by committee at a giant publishing house. Don’t get me wrong—if a major publisher came along tomorrow with a sign-on deal, I’d take it in a heartbeat! But as an indie, you get pure, unadulterated story (and my own questionable line-editing—sorry about that!).

I truly love writing these books and bringing big, wild ideas to life. I have so many manuscripts in progress—some partially complete, some just a single paragraph, and others waiting in the wings. I can’t wait over the next few years to get every single one of them out to you.

Thank you for reading, please continue to enjoy the journey, and if you ever have any feedback, I’d love to hear from you.

Send me a message ↗

The people behind the pages

None of this would have been possible without the love and support of my wonderful fiancée, my amazing stepson and especially my beautiful daughter. At three days old, she suffered a neonatal stroke and now lives with epilepsy and cerebral palsy. Her strength, determination and courage inspire me every day.

“Limitations are the ones you set yourself.”

The ideas behind the books

Every story starts
somewhere.

A documentary. A game. A recurring dream. In my own words, here’s how those first ideas became the worlds in my books.

A question about survival

The Continuity series

Documentaries such as Evacuate Earth and How the Universe Works got me thinking about how humanity might survive a disaster on a planetary scale. One question stayed with me: what would happen if a black hole passed through our solar system, and how would ordinary people cope?

I began imagining the story almost like a film in my head: a changing world, families trying to reach safety, and the decisions humanity would have to make to survive. Those ideas became Continuity. Seeing that imagined world become a complete trilogy is something I’m very proud of.

Explore the trilogy →

Beyond the familiar universe

The Rubin Anomaly series

Watching The Twilight Zone and the 1990s series Sliders fed my fascination with strange realities and worlds beyond our own. Ideas about multiple universes added to that curiosity: what might exist beyond the universe we know?

I wanted to explore that sense of wonder and unease through a story of my own. The Rubin Anomaly grew from those questions, and from imagining how people might react when the familiar rules of their world begin to change.

Explore The Rubin Anomaly →

What about the Navy?

The Last Fleet: When the Flags Fell

This is my personal favourite of my novels. Playing the original Resident Evil on the PlayStation, watching Night of the Living Dead, and later enjoying World War Z and The Walking Dead all helped spark the idea.

I kept coming back to one question: what about the Navy? If an outbreak overwhelmed the land, could warships at sea offer a chance of survival? I wanted to explore what happened to those crews, how they might help others, and whether staying offshore would really be enough. That question became The Last Fleet, and I wanted to share it to see whether other readers had wondered the same thing.

Explore The Last Fleet →

From a recurring dream

The Last Orbits of Man: Descent

For years—starting back when I was a teenager—I had this recurring dream where I was the brave action hero caught in a mashup of zombies and space warfare. Earth was completely overrun by these creatures, and at the same time, humanity was fighting off the Bakali: a brutal warrior race inspired by a combination of the Klingons and the Hirogen from Star Trek.

Eventually, I thought to myself: I can make them even scarier.

So, I set out to write a novel built directly from those literal dreams. I have to say, taking those late-night ideas and turning them into Descent has made it one of my absolute personal favourites to write.

Next on the horizon.

New worlds are taking shape. Here’s what I’m working on next.

01 In development

World Undone · Standalone novel

The Last Broadcast: When the World Went Silent

Former Marine Ryan Hudson moved to Sitka, Alaska, hoping for a quieter life. But when a deadly outbreak spreads across the mainland and broadcasts begin to fall silent, the remote fishing community faces the possibility that help will never come.

Cut off from the outside world, Ryan and the people of Sitka must find a way to protect their home as civilisation collapses.

The Last Broadcast: When the World Went Silent is a standalone survival thriller in the World Undone series, set in the same world as The Last Fleet.
